parakeet: Belief in the end times does not stay in the realm of private spirituality. It reshapes how people think about politics, responsibility, and the future. If people are convinced that the world is about to end, then long horizon ethical concerns, things like protecting the environment, strengthening institutions, investing in education, or building sustainable communities can start to feel spiritually optional. Why pour energy into repairing a world you believe is about to be destroyed? That kind of thinking creates short-termism, where urgency replaces stewardship and immediate ideological battles matter more than the long-term health of society. It also creates a dangerous permission structure for authoritarianism. When people are trained to see the world as a cosmic battle between God's side and the beast system, strongman leaders can be reframed as necessary weapons in that fight. A leader does not need to be morally healthy, compassionate, or even consistent. They only need to appear powerful enough to oppose the right enemies. In that framework, cruelty can look like courage, domination can look like righteousness, and abuse of power can be excused as part of God's larger plan. That is one of the most socially destabilizing effects of apocalyptic belief. It can make people more willing to trade ethics for perceived protection. On top of that, end times thinking tends to fracture communities from the inside. It intensifies boundary policing, where the central question becomes who is truly faithful and who has been compromised. People begin sorting each other into categories who's real, who's deceived, who's worldly, who's Babylon. Instead of building trust, nuance, and shared responsibility, the culture becomes more suspicious, more combative, and more obsessed with purity. In that environment, disagreement stops being a normal part of communal life and starts being treated as evidence of corruption. The result is a society that becomes easier to divide, easier to manipulate, and far less capable of working together for anything larger than survival and ideological control.
